# Diagnosing Memory Leaks in a Long-Running Python HTTP Server

## 1. Reproduce & Establish Baseline

### 1.1 Confirm the leak exists
```bash
# Run your integration test suite with memory tracking enabled
python -X tracemalloc=25 my_integration_tests.py --duration 3600

# Or use a simple wrapper to track RSS over time:
#!/bin/bash
# monitor_rss.sh
PID=$1
while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; do
    RSS=$(ps -o rss= -p $PID)
    echo "$(date +%s) $RSS" >> /tmp/rss_$PID.log
    sleep 5
done
```

### 1.2 Establish baseline memory behavior
```bash
# Run a short, clean session and record memory
python -m tracemalloc my_server.py --port 8080 &
SERVER_PID=$!

# Make a few requests to warm up caches
for i in $(seq 1 100); do
    curl -s http://localhost:8080/health > /dev/null
done

# Record baseline after warm-up
python3 -c "
import psutil, sys
proc = psutil.Process($SERVER_PID)
mem = proc.memory_info()
print(f'Baseline RSS: {mem.rss / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB')
print(f'Baseline VMS: {mem.vms / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MB')
"

# Kill the server
kill $SERVER_PID
```

---

## 2. Profiling with `tracemalloc` (Built-in, Low Overhead)

### 2.1 Enable tracemalloc in your server entry point
```python
# my_server.py
import tracemalloc
import atexit

# Start tracing at the very beginning of main()
def main():
    tracemalloc.start(25)  # Keep up to 25 frames for each trace
    
    @atexit.register
    def dump_traces():
        snapshot = tracemalloc.take_snapshot()
        top_stats = snapshot.statistics('lineno')
        
        print("\n=== TOP 10 MEMORY ALLOCATIONS BY LINE ===")
        for stat in top_stats[:10]:
            print
